haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC. It extracts orders with updated_at after W minus 2 h, up to the replica clock at snapshot start.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open up to 90 min, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit. So a row can appear up to 90 min after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: Every app write bumps updated_at. The next night extracts the changed row again, and the MERGE replaces the older version in fact_orders.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at, a soft delete. The next night extracts it, and the fact_orders row gets is_deleted = true. No row is removed.
haiku-low.q5: Nothing commits to fact_orders or W. The run is marked failed and retried after 15 min, up to 3 attempts per night. After the third failure, on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed fact_orders, not partial data. A staleness alert is posted to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: Sunday's reconciliation finds the mismatch on the order's creation day, since it was created in the last 30 days. It then reloads that day.
haiku-low.q8: The conditional MERGE on order_id inserts when there is no match. It updates only when the staged updated_at is newer and skips otherwise, so each order_id has one row.
haiku-low.q9: It is stored in etl_watermark as W, the extract upper bound of the last successful attempt. It is written in Step 5, in the same transaction as the MERGE, at commit.
haiku-low.q10: Step 5 is one warehouse transaction holding the MERGE, the W update and the succeeded run status. Dashboards see all of it or none of it.
haiku-low.q11: The staged data is discarded: the next attempt truncates stg_orders. The retry reads the same W, extracts from W minus 2 h, and takes a fresh upper bound.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads every order created on a mismatched day, after truncating stg_orders. It applies the same conditional MERGE in its own transaction. It does not change W.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica orders with updated_at after lower (W minus 2 h) up to upper (replica clock at snapshot start), in one read snapshot; includes soft-deleted ones (is_deleted = deleted_at is not null).
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open for up to 90 min, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit, so the row can appear on the replica up to 90 min after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: Every app write bumps updated_at, so the next night's extract picks the changed row up again; the MERGE updates fact_orders because the staged updated_at is newer.
sonnet.q4: Deletes are soft: the app sets deleted_at (a write that bumps updated_at). The next extract brings it as is_deleted = true and the MERGE updates the fact_orders row. No row is ever removed from fact_orders.
sonnet.q5: Nothing is committed to fact_orders or W. The etl_runs row is marked failed. If fewer than 3 attempts tonight, wait 15 min and start a new attempt; after the third failure, on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards keep showing the last committed fact_orders (no partial night). A staleness alert is posted to the #data-alerts channel (no succeeded etl_runs row for tonight). A load committing after 06:00 is kept.
sonnet.q7: The next Sunday reconciliation: it compares the last 30 order-creation days (row count and checksum of order_id + updated_at) replica vs fact_orders, finds the mismatch on the order's creation day, and reloads that day.
sonnet.q8: The MERGE on order_id is conditional: no match inserts; match with staged updated_at newer updates; match not newer is skipped. So each order_id keeps one row with the latest version.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl_watermark (one row, W). It is set to upper (the replica clock at snapshot start of the successful attempt), inside the step 5 transaction together with the MERGE and marking the etl_runs row succeeded, committed at once.
sonnet.q10: Step 5 is a single warehouse transaction (MERGE, W update, run status), committed at once, and dashboards read only fact_orders (never stg_orders), so they see all of a night's changes or none.
sonnet.q11: The failed attempt's committed nothing; stg_orders is truncated at the start of the next attempt, discarding the staged data. The retry reads the same W, so lower = W minus 2 h, with a fresh upper bound taken at its new snapshot start.
sonnet.q12: It truncates stg_orders and re-extracts every order created on a mismatched day (from the replica), applies them with the same conditional MERGE in its own transaction, and does not change W.
